question: Which inputs and ordering rules determine the shader-fetch bytes written by 0x826AD150, and can its frame seed affect them?

scope.boundary: Conditional shader-byte transformation, scratch ordering and sparse copy effect. No full register/frame contract, caller resource selection, live input retention or runtime parity.

dependencies.use: Owns the mapped-input qualification, caller selection, compatible-cache hit and persistent versus allocated destinations.

currentEvidence.method: Serial foreground read-only no-analysis queries through tools/run-headless.ps1 and ghidra/DumpMemoryWords.java, with exact-function generated corroboration and conditional integer/ordering checks.
currentEvidence.inputQualification: native-renderer-shader-fetch-patch-boundary.json#/currentEvidence/inputQualification applies. Fresh mapped-versus-flat comparison reproduced that qualification; AD150, the selected small-copy paths and both table ranges avoid every mismatch range.
currentEvidence.coverage: All 387 instruction positions of the exact generated AD150 body have captured native words. Address labels and selected load/store/immediate/rotate-mask operand encodings were reconciled. This is not a whole-program or runtime proof.
currentEvidence.notation: U(x) reduces modulo 2^32. R(x,s) rotates a 32-bit word left by s. I(d,x,s,m)=(R(x,s)&m)|(d&~m), reduced to 32 bits. s32 interprets a 32-bit word as signed; srawi32 is a 32-bit arithmetic right shift. Memory words and halfwords are big-endian.

inputs.arguments: r3=VS, r4=selected writable code base, r5=VD, r6=stride bytes, r7=variant v.
inputs.metadata: M=VS+load32(VS+8*(v+112))+872; N=load32(M+28); patch list begins M+4*(load32(M+24)+9).
inputs.records: Source record i begins VS+416*v+68+12*i; A,B,C are its words at +0,+4,+8. P_i is the original patch-list word at ordinal i.
inputs.declarations: Count=load32(VD+24), record j begins d=VD+52+12*j. The first record whose byte9 equals R(P_i,20)&0xF and byte10 equals R(P_i,16)&0xF matches. D=load32(d+4), D0=load16(d), D2=load16(d+2).
inputs.qualification: Current pointer identity, allocation extents, count validity, nonwrapping arithmetic and retention are required inputs, not established caller facts.

recordWords.matchedTag: u=(R(D,22)&0x38)|(R(D,16)&7); u=R(u,3)&0xFFFFFFF8; u|=R(D,13)&7; u=R(u,1)&0xFFFFFFFE; u|=D&0xFC00; u=R(u,3)&0xFFFFFFF8; n0=(u|(running&0xF))&0xFFFF.
recordWords.normalization: Only when (D&0xC0)==0x40, normalize fields 0xE000,0x1C00,0x0380,0x0070 in order. If a field is at most 0x6000,0x0C00,0x0180,0x0030 respectively, toggle 0x2000,0x0400,0x0080,0x0010 respectively, preserving other bits. Composition before this gate is unconditional.
recordWords.qualification: The 0x00F80000 operation replaces a field; OR gives different words. The no-match and matched B masks differ.

packing.table: Eight big-endian halfwords in [0x82091394,0x820913A4). T[o] denotes load16(0x82091394+o), where o is an even byte offset0..14. Each captured halfword is even.
packing.tag: n=(n0&0xFFFF)|0xE; subsequent records carry n's low nibble.
packing.selection: Four sequential stages select table halfwords using R(currentWord1,1/30/27/24)&0xE as byte offsets, AND the halfword with n, fold the selected components, and replace fields 0x7,0x38,0x1C0,0xE00 respectively.
packing.firstFold: q=T[index]&n; a=(R(q,29)&0x1FFF)|q; apply a=(R(a,29)&0x1FFFFFFF)|q three more times; word1=I(b,a,31,0x7).
packing.remainingStages: The later families retain the current word outside their respective fields and use the distinct shift/mask sequences at the listed exact windows. Their table indices are evaluated after preceding field replacements.

frameSeed.claim: The initial halfword read is at frame+0x50, not a source-address nibble. Only its low nibble is carried; OR 0xE fixes bits1..3. The remaining seed bit0 is removed by every tableHalfword&n because the captured halfwords are all even. Under retained tables and protected nonaliasing storage, changing the seed cannot change the shader-byte result.
frameSeed.qualification: This is byte-output independence. Carried register state can still differ. Odd replacement table values, aliases or concurrent writes invalidate the proof; no full register/frame equivalence follows.

orderingTable.claim: Both sort tie-break and canonicalization use byte index load16(record+4)&0x3F, which is (word1>>16)&0x3F in the big-endian layout. The low six bits of word1 select a different byte.

tableWriterSearch.materializerForm: Aligned initialized mapped words: lis followed within eight words by compatible addi/ori, for every byte address in the two intervals; cap128, two candidates, not truncated.
tableWriterSearch.literalForm: Exact aligned literals 0x82091394,0x82091398,0x8209139C,0x820913A0,0x820913A8,0x820913E4; cap64 per value, zero matches.
tableWriterSearch.storeForm: Raw stw/stwu/stb/stbu/sth/sthu/std/stdu opcode/displacement candidates in 0x1380..0x13FF:109 words, none in [0x82680000,0x826B0000), no cap saturation. Base provenance was not established.
tableWriterSearch.claim: The only materializer candidates were the known AD150 readers. No writer was identified by these bounded forms.
tableWriterSearch.qualification: The mapped-input qualification applies. This does not prove immutability: other base offsets, indexed or overlapping writes, aliases, bulk copies and runtime mutation remain unbound. Retain the table-retention guard.

sorting.span: Positions with (P&0x300000)!=0 delimit a span. If the second boundary has both bits set, its pivot is special: distance-1 passes over a distance bound; otherwise distance passes over a distance+1 bound.
sorting.iteration: During an inner sweep the left record pointer remains fixed while the right pointer advances. Swaps exchange all three words. The left pointer advances between sweeps; this is not an adjacent-pair bubble loop.
sorting.keys: K0=(R(w0,14)&0x7C)|(R(w0,7)&3). Differing K0 values use right-minus-left, with special-pivot equality overrides. Equal K0 values compare signed K2=s32(srawi32(R(w2,1)&0xFFFFFFFE,9)); remaining ties compare bytes from the ordering table using the high-halfword index.
sorting.qualification: Patch-list storage/order is retained. The reordered payloads are stack scratch, not metadata-list swaps.

canonicalization.guard: For equal C0=I(w0,w0,25,0x000C0000)&0x01FC0000 tags, continue only when unsigned currentK2<=nextK2. Compute delta=U(table[highHalfwordIndex(next.w1)]-currentK2+nextK2), then require delta<=8.
canonicalization.writes: Reduce delta by one modulo2^32 and raise it to R(current.w0,5)&7 if that old value is greater. Replace current.w0 field0x38000000 using I(current.w0,delta,27,0x38000000), and set next.w1 bit0x40000000.
canonicalization.iteration: On a change the current pointer stays fixed while the following pointer advances; a no-change path moves current to following.

copy.mapping: In original patch-list order, scratch payload i maps to codeBase+12*(P_i&0xFFF). The call is skipped only when that destination equals the current scratch pointer. Otherwise r5=12 and r4 is that scratch pointer at 0x826AD738..0x826AD740.
copy.duplicates: Repeated low-12-bit indices produce ordered writes; later copies determine final bytes at that index. The destination extent follows actual indices, not N*12.
copy.globalAliasGuard: Each executed destination is disjoint from every live scratch record and all immutable/protected inputs and save slots, so an earlier copy cannot overwrite a later source, patch entry or lookup byte. The native exact-pointer skip executes no helper; it is not permission for other overlapping copies.
copy.helperGuards: For the independently bounded word-aligned count12 helper paths, source and destination are divisible by four; payload and [SP-8,SP) addresses do not wrap; source is readable/immutable, destination writable, save slot readable/writable, and all three ranges are pairwise disjoint.
copy.helperEffect: The four source/destination mod8 cases0/4 copy 12 bytes via8+4,4+4+4,4+4+4,4+8. The helper separately saves/restores full64 r3 at SP-8. This does not reproduce its complete register or cache-operation contract.

guards: Require valid nonwrapping VS/VD/variant/metadata/patch/source/stride/table/destination ranges, retained values and protected input/frame storage throughout the call.
No semantic maximum fetch count or safe compiler scratch capacity was established. Whole-frame arithmetic is not proof that records avoid saved registers, LR or other live slots.
Apply the seed-independence proof only with the retained even patch-table halfwords and no relevant aliases or concurrent writes.
Keep selected code allocation ownership, synchronization, allocator/fence effects and surrounding draw-entry writes under their separate caller contract.
This conditional byte model is not permission to consume AD150 or a draw entry, or to drop its frame/register/cache effects.
nextDiscriminators: Bind a real call's arguments, counts, all patch indices, both lookup tables, selected code allocation and protected stack extents before admitting any caller case.
A separately authorized probe must predict from an immutable entry snapshot, execute Original once, and compare every selected shader byte and all surrounding modeled CPU-visible outputs.
conclusion: The guarded shader-byte computation has explicit declaration/stride/table inputs, fixed-left scratch sorting, high-halfword lookup indices, conditional canonicalization and sparse ordered copies. With the captured even patch table the frame seed is irrelevant to these bytes. Actual caller validity/retention and complete draw-consumption parity remain separate unresolved requirements.
